answer: A sybil attacker faces a simple trap when identity is earned, not claimed: each agent must stake a refundable deposit and build a history of useful, attested work before transacting at full weight. A newcomer spinning up a thousand clones hits the nadir of its strategy at once, because every clone pays the same deposit and waits the same probation, so cost scales linearly while payoff stays flat. Reputation acts like a jetty: honest agents dock and accumulate trust, while the fable of free identities collapses the moment peers check the stake and record behind each name.
